SEORI AND G. BHAUMIK Botanical S m y of Indio, SMtong NEW DISTRIBUTIONAL RECORD OF PTERNOPETALUM TANAKAE (F'RANCH. & SAV.) HAND.-MAZZT. FROM BHUTAN The genus Pternopetalurn with about 27 species is mainly Chinese in distribution, extending to Nepal in the West and Japan in the East. Of the three species recorded so far from India, P. senii Deb & Dutta is reported from Tirap district in Arunachal Pradesh, P. radiatum (W. Smith) P. Mukh. grows in Yeumrong and Sebu Valley in Sikkim and P. vulgare (Dunn) Hand.- Mazzt. has been collected 'from Kameng district in Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur and Nepal. The present authors came across a speci- men collected from Bhutan, which on es- amination against specimens and literatures is identified as Pternopeta~urn tanakne (Franch. & Sav.) Hand.-Mazzt This sFe. cies was earlier reported from Japan, Cen- tral China and Korea. A close affinity exists Datc of *ceipt t 18,8,77, Datc of acceptance : 16, 12. 77 between Umbellifers from China and Hima- layas, particularly of Eastern Himalayas- A brief description of the species is given below : Plants slender, 10-15 cm long, most- ly simple; glabrous. Leaves few, basal ones ovate-deltoid in outline, 1-2.5 cm in diam., ternate pinnate ; leaflets ovate orbicular, 5-10 mm long and broad, serrate to deeply incised. caulin; leaves . pinnateiy divided. Involucre absent. Rays slender 4-10, 1-3 cm long, spreading. Pedicels mostly 2, very unequal, 0-1 -5 mm. Involucel of I -2 setiform bractlets, to 1.5 mm. Sepals not evident. Petals ovate acuminate but apex not inflexed. Fruit oblong ovoid, 1.5 to 2 mm long, ribs obscure, stylopodium low conic. Specimen referred : Between GyasaDmng and Laya, Mo Chu, 3,200 m. Ludlow, G. She# 6 1. Hicks, 16554 (C AL).
